question: How does Sensible OCR behave on a mixed PDF where some pages are digitally generated and others are scanned — do preprocessors apply uniformly?

fetched_pages.title: OCR
fetched_pages.content:
When you extract document data with Sensible, Sensible automatically performs optical character recognition (OCR) on the document for you, except in advanced cases. If the document doesn't require OCR, Sensible automatically extracts embedded text directly from the document to optimize performance.

For advanced cases, you can configure how Sensible OCRs documents using the following parameters:

- OCR Level parameter (configurable for document types): Use this option to configure the criteria by which Sensible determines if a whole document requires OCR.
- OCR preprocessor (configurable for configs): Use this option to OCR specified pages or page ranges in a document.
- OCR Engine parameter (configurable for document types): Use this option to choose your OCR provider, for example, Amazon, Google, or Microsoft.

For an overview of how Sensible handles OCR for supported file types, see the following steps:

1. Sensible converts several file types to PDFs.
2. For file types that contain embedded text (for example, digital PDFs), Sensible extracts the text directly. If it completes this step, it skips the following steps.
3. For file types that lack embedded text, Sensible transforms the bytes of the document into raw text, and determines whether the document needs OCR:
   - If the file type is an image (for example, PNG), Sensible runs OCR for the whole document.
   - (Configurable) If the file is a PDF, Sensible processes the file using heuristics to determine if the whole document needs OCR. Configure this step using the document type's OCR Level parameter and OCR Engine.
4. (Configurable) After additional intervening steps, Sensible applies your configured preprocessors, including the OCR preprocessor. This preprocessor runs for documents that don't trigger whole-document OCR in a previous step.

Notes:
- For more information about OCR versus embedded text extraction, see Solving direct text extraction from PDFs.
- For information about extracting data from non-text images, such as photographs, charts, or illustrations, see the Query Group method's Multimodal Engine parameter.

fetched_pages.title: Extracting handwriting and OCR text
fetched_pages.content:
Best practices for OCR and handwriting extraction.

OCR tips: Sensible provides confidence scores for OCR'd text in the extraction when you configure high verbosity, so you know whether the extracted output comes from high- or low-quality text images. For document types that use OCR, write validations to warn you about extractions from low-quality scans.

Handwriting tips:
- Choosing an OCR engine: Choose Google OCR.
- Defining regions: Handwriting can occupy an unpredictable region or even overlap other lines. To capture handwriting, Sensible recommends defining a region with a small height and long width that runs through the middle of the area that can contain the handwriting.
- Correcting for vertical misalignment: Jitter in the vertical positions of handwritten lines can cause Sensible to incorrectly sort lines that a human reader interprets as following left to right. The Sort Lines parameter corrects this problem.

fetched_pages.title: OCR preprocessor
Preprocessors
fetched_pages.content:
Transform documents before extraction. Use the following preprocessors to clean up your documents before extracting structured data. Preprocessors execute in the order you define them in an array.

Available preprocessors include: Deskew, Ligature, Linearize, Merge Lines, Multicolumn, NLP, OCR, Page Range, Remove Header, Remove Footer, Remove Lines, Remove Page, Rotate page, Scale, Split Lines.

The OCR preprocessor: Selectively OCRs pages in documents containing a mix of digitally generated text and text images (such as scanned text). If the whole PDF is a scan, you don't need to configure this preprocessor.

fetched_pages.title: Deskew
fetched_pages.content:
Use this preprocessor to deskew documents in advanced cases where Sensible doesn't automatically correct the alignment of text in documents. ID cards and receipts are documents that can often be skewed, for example as a result of being photographed at an angle instead of straight on.

Parameters:
- type (required): 'deskew'
- fixedPoints (required): Deskews the text in a skewed document by mapping the positions of three skewed points to their ideal positions in an unskewed document.
- matchAll (Boolean, default false): If true, deskews all pages containing the lines specified by the Fixed Points parameter.
- start ('left' or 'right', default 'left'): Specifies whether the Fixed Point is at the upper-left or upper-right corner of the anchor line's boundaries.

Notes on page transformation preprocessors:
- Deskew: Handles complex page transformations (affine), requires advanced configuration.
- Rotate Page: Sensible corrects rotation automatically in most cases. If it doesn't, configure the Rotate Page preprocessor.
- Scale: Use as an easier-to-configure alternative to Deskew if only scale is affected.
